title: A Chemically Grounded Evaluation Framework for Generative Models in Materials Discovery
experiments_summary: The study employs two main approaches to generate candidate materials for evaluation: (1) a perturbative approach and (2) a generative model approach. In the perturbative approach, known materials from the Materials Project (MP) and OQMD databases are modified using three perturbation strategies—atomic position perturbations, lattice parameter perturbations, and combined perturbations—each applied at three intensity levels (small, medium, large), with specific displacement and angular tolerances defined for each level. In the generative model approach, three diffusion-based models—CDVAE, GemsDiff, and DiffCSP—are retrained from scratch using preprocessed MP and OQMD datasets filtered to retain metastable structures with formation energy below 0.1 eV/atom and up to 64 atoms per structure, yielding datasets of up to 87k (MP) and 221k (OQMD) structures. All generated structures undergo a DFT-based screening pipeline implemented via VASP, using PAW pseudopotentials with the PBE-GGA functional. Static DFT calculations are performed using the MPStaticSet configuration to obtain total energies for SUN metric computation over 1024 structures, while DFT relaxation via MPRelaxSet is used to compute RMSD on 64 structures due to higher computational cost. Gaussian smearing (ISMEAR=0) is applied instead of the default tetrahedron method to accommodate diverse material types. Pre-simulation processing includes duplicate filtering via pymatgen's StructureMatcher (with tolerances of 20% for lattice lengths, 30% for atomic coordinates, and 5 degrees for lattice angles), exclusion of noble gases, f-block elements, and structures with interatomic distances below 0.5 Å. Post-simulation steps include space group analysis via SpacegroupAnalyzer/spglib and convex hull construction for energy-above-hull calculations. Band gaps are estimated using the Delta-Sol semi-empirical method. Evaluation metrics computed include RMSD, SUN (Stability, Uniqueness, Novelty), Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) over properties such as density and formation energy, validity, and latent-space coverage metrics (precision, recall) using CrystalNN fingerprints and Fréchet distance. All metrics are compared across both the perturbative and generative model conditions to assess their sensitivity and alignment with physical feasibility.
